one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: One of the fastest growing branded packaged spices and food companies among the Key Packaged Spices Peers, leading in Madhya Pradesh with a 20.7% value share in Fiscal 2025 and a growing pan-India footprint under the 'Pushp' and 'Munimji' brands.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Pushp Brand (India) Limited is a branded packaged spices and food company offering pure spices, blended spices and adjacent products such as soya products and tea, sold under the premium 'Pushp' brand and the popular-category 'Munimji' brand. Founded in 1974 in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, it manufactures at two fully automated ISO-certified facilities in Indore and sells to Indian households through general trade, modern trade, e-commerce, quick-commerce and HoReCa channels. Products are available across 24 states and union territories, with an established presence in Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan and growing scale in Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and Gujarat.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- A91 Emerging Fund I LLP — Investor Selling Shareholder: Marquee investor (A91 Partners); offering up to 4,220,000 Equity Shares of face value of ₹5 each in the Offer for Sale
- Sixth Sense India Opportunities III — Investor Selling Shareholder: Marquee investor (Sixth Sense Ventures); offering up to 1,545,000 Equity Shares of face value of ₹5 each in the Offer for Sale
- Munimji Foods and Spices Private Limited — Other directorship of both Promoters: Unlisted Indian company in which Mahendra Kumar Surana and Surendra Kumar Surana are directors
- Munimji Exports Private Limited — Other directorship of both Promoters: Unlisted Indian company in which Mahendra Kumar Surana and Surendra Kumar Surana are directors
- Pushp Foundation — Section 8 company under the Companies Act: Both Promoters are directors of this Section 8 company
- Pragati Graphics Private Limited — Job-work counterparty: The Company has entered into job-work arrangements to utilise its Rangwasa Facility, Indore for packaging of soya and tea products; installed capacity 3,000 MT as of March 31, 2026
- The Knowledge Company LLP — Commissioned industry report provider: Prepared the 'Industry Report on the Packaged Spices Market in India' dated May 23, 2026 (the TKC Report), exclusively commissioned and paid for by the Company in connection with the Offer

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward linkage is via a direct, origin-linked procurement model rather than owned agricultural assets: raw materials are sourced from established suppliers across key spice-producing belts spanning Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan, supplemented by procurement through major trading hubs including Indore, Mumbai, Delhi, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Siliguri; procurement is typically aligned to harvest windows so as to source the right varietals and grades at the appropriate time for quality and pricing. Superior-quality hing is procured through international import channels via one of the Company's domestic suppliers. The DRHP states this model provides greater control over the quality, consistency and cost of raw materials and helps mitigate adulteration risks. Manufacturing is in-house at the two fully automated, ISO-certified facilities at Bardari and Bharosala in Indore, using vertical flow technology and automated process controls, with integrated cold-storage and warehousing infrastructure and in-house testing laboratories; packaging of soya and tea products is outsourced under job-work arrangements to Pragati Graphics Private Limited at its Rangwasa facility in Indore (Pragati Graphics and Packaging Private Limited also appears among the Fiscal 2025 top-10 suppliers). Forward integration runs through a Company-controlled route to market: logistics and warehousing infrastructure integrated with the Indore manufacturing operations, SAP-enabled logistics and inventory management systems, sales force automation and distributor management systems, an owned fleet of vehicles for transportation of finished goods to nearby locations and key logistics hubs (reducing dependence on third-party freight for last-mile delivery within core markets), a staged super-stockist-to-C&F distribution model for new states, and an owned direct-to-consumer online store, 'Pushp Online'. Supplier dependence has fallen over the period: purchases from the largest supplier were 17.34%, 16.08% and 6.49% of total purchases in Fiscals 2024, 2025 and 2026, and from the top 10 suppliers 55.12%, 51.36% and 45.72%.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Mix shift towards blended spices and other value-added products, which carry higher product margins than pure spices - Fiscal 2026 product margins were 35.31% for pure spices, 43.75% for blended spices and 25.98% for other products
- Overall Product Margin improved from 31.91% (FY2024) to 35.10% (FY2025) to 37.76% (FY2026), with EBITDA Margin moving from 12.32% to 15.92% to 17.16%
- Volume-led growth: year-on-year volume growth of 2.49% (FY2024), 10.63% (FY2025) and 14.47% (FY2026) against revenue growth of 17.79%, 1.61% and 19.10%
- Direct, origin-linked procurement from established suppliers plus major trading hubs (Indore, Mumbai, Delhi, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Siliguri) provides control over raw material quality, consistency and cost
- Distribution reach and rural penetration outside Madhya Pradesh, enabled by sales force automation and distributor management systems, supports availability-led revenue growth
- Light balance sheet: finance cost of ₹ 14.21 million in FY2026 on current borrowings of ₹ 193.71 million against total equity of ₹ 3,063.39 million, supporting ROCE of 24.70% and ROE of 21.40%
- Automation-led manufacturing and standardized quality control with capacity utilization at 38.95% as at March 31, 2026, leaving operating leverage available
- Note: the MD&A section in the routed extract is limited to its preamble; drivers above are drawn from the 'Our Business' key financial and operational table and its notes

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Continue the journey from a regional presence to a pan-India brand, having expanded over the last five years into states such as Telangana, Goa and Tamil Nadu
- Expand into new geographies supported by structured distributor onboarding, data-driven territory planning and targeted rural penetration, enabled by sales force automation and distributor management systems
- Progressively expand the revenue mix towards blended spices and other value-added products, which typically command higher product margins than pure spices
- Grow the multi-channel approach across general trade, modern trade, e-commerce, quick-commerce and the HoReCa sector
- Continue targeted brand-building through celebrity engagement, national television and cinema advertising, digital outreach and in-store branding

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company operates two fully automated, ISO-certified facilities at Bardari and Bharosala in Indore, Madhya Pradesh with an aggregate installed capacity of 60,000 MT per annum and a capacity utilization rate of 37.19% as of March 31, 2026, sited in proximity to major spice-producing belts in Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Rajasthan. Total installed capacity (including the 3,000 MT job-work Rangwasa Facility) rose from 53,000 MT as at March 31, 2024 and March 31, 2025 to 63,000 MT as at March 31, 2026, while capacity utilization was 36.49%, 39.07% and 38.95% across those years, leaving headroom for volume growth. Capacity is supported by vertical flow technology and automated process controls, integrated cold-storage and warehousing infrastructure and in-house testing laboratories; packaging of soya and tea products is carried out under job-work arrangements at the Rangwasa Facility of Pragati Graphics Private Limited. Distribution expansion runs in parallel: retail touchpoints grew from over 237,000 (FY2024) to over 368,000 (FY2026), and distributors from 853 as at March 31, 2024 to 1,016 as at March 31, 2026 (CAGR 9.14%), with distributors outside Madhya Pradesh rising from 642 to 752 (CAGR 8.23%), supported by two C&F agents and a 732-person sales and channel management workforce.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Pan-India player with leadership position in West and Central India
- Diversified and expanding product portfolio with innovative offerings
- Established and scalable distribution network
- Robust sourcing capabilities and strategically located manufacturing facilities
- Strong liquidity position with a track record of consistent financial performance
- Experienced Promoters and senior management team, backed by marquee investors
- Over five decades of operating history and a nationally recognized brand, with a 20.7% value share in Madhya Pradesh, approximately 58% of the state's packaged hing market and approximately 22.3% of packaged vegetarian spices in Fiscal 2025 (Source: TKC Report)
- Direct, origin-linked procurement model spanning Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan, giving greater control over quality, consistency and cost of raw materials

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Product concentration in the 'pure spices' category (chilli, coriander and turmeric) — Pure spices contributed 63.56%, 63.59% and 62.20% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; the DRHP's first internal risk factor states that an inability to anticipate and adapt to evolving consumer tastes in this category may impact demand and adversely affect business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
- Geographic concentration in Madhya Pradesh and adjacent West and Central India states — Leadership rests on a 20.7% Madhya Pradesh value share and approximately 58% of the state's packaged hing market; of 1,016 distributors as at March 31, 2026 only 752 sit outside Madhya Pradesh, so the pan-India ambition is still unproven at scale.
- Dependence on agricultural raw material sourcing and the procurement network — The direct, origin-linked model draws raw materials from Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan plus trading hubs; quality, consistency and cost of these spices flow directly into Product Margin, which is the primary earnings lever.
- Low capacity utilisation — Utilisation was 38.95% as at March 31, 2026 (37.19% for the two owned facilities) against 63,000 MT of installed capacity, so absorption of fixed manufacturing cost depends on volume growth still to be delivered.
- Reliance on a third-party job-work facility for adjacent categories — Soya and tea products are packaged at the 3,000 MT Rangwasa Facility under job-work arrangements with Pragati Graphics Private Limited, leaving the newest categories dependent on an external counterparty.
- Market and share claims rest on a paid, commissioned industry report — The TKC Report dated May 23, 2026 was exclusively commissioned and paid for by the Company in connection with the Offer, and the DRHP itself carries a risk factor that reliance on such information for an investment decision is subject to inherent risks.
- Use of non-GAAP financial measures — Product Margin, EBITDA, EBITDA Margin, ROCE and ROE presented in the DRHP are not measures of operating performance or liquidity defined by Ind AS and the manner of calculation may vary from that used by other companies, limiting comparability.
- Distribution reach and brand spend dependence — Growth is carried by 368,000+ retail touchpoints, 1,016 distributors, two C&F agents and a 732-person sales and channel management workforce, plus celebrity-led advertising, all of which require continuing investment to sustain availability and recall.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Continue the transition from a regional Madhya Pradesh presence to a pan-India brand, having already reached 24 states and union territories and entered Telangana, Goa and Tamil Nadu over the last five years.**
- **Keep expanding the distributor network into new geographies, particularly outside Madhya Pradesh, through structured distributor onboarding, data-driven territory planning and targeted rural penetration.**
- **Continue expanding the revenue mix towards blended spices and other value-added products, which typically command higher product margins than pure spices.**
- **Ramp utilisation of the 63,000 MT installed capacity across the Bardari, Bharosala and job-work Rangwasa Facilities, which stood at 38.95% overall (37.19% for the two owned facilities) as at March 31, 2026.**
- **Installed capacity was raised from 53,000 MT as at March 31, 2025 to 63,000 MT as at March 31, 2026, including the 3,000 MT job-work Rangwasa Facility taken on for packaging soya and tea products.**
- **Extend into adjacent packaged food categories beyond spices, having launched tea products in April 2026 alongside the existing soya products business.**
- **Expand the multi-channel footprint across modern trade, e-commerce, quick-commerce and the HoReCa sector alongside the general trade base of over 368,000 retail touchpoints.**
- **Sustain a targeted brand-building programme using celebrity engagement (Ajay Devgan, Tamanna Bhatia), national television and cinema advertising, digital outreach and in-store branding under the 'Purity That's Forever' and 'Swad ka …**
- **The Offer is entirely an Offer for Sale of up to 7,445,000 Equity Shares of face value of ₹5 each by the Selling Shareholders; the Company will not receive any proceeds and the only objects are the OFS and achieving the benefits of listing.**
- **Promoters Mahendra Kumar Surana and Surendra Kumar Surana each offer up to 840,000 Equity Shares while investors A91 Emerging Fund I LLP and Sixth Sense India Opportunities III offer up to 4,220,000 and 1,545,000 Equity Shares …**
- **Management explicitly flags significant dependence on the pure spices category (chilli, coriander and turmeric) and the risk of failing to anticipate and adapt to evolving consumer tastes in that category.**
- **Management flags that the TKC Report underpinning the DRHP's market share and growth claims was exclusively commissioned and paid for by the Company in connection with the Offer, and that reliance on it for an investment decision is …**
